column4: Jesus is the Way, the Truth, and the Life (John 14:6), fully embodying God’s truth, wisdom, and revelation. This embodiment, the Word (logos), existed from the beginning and became flesh to dwell among us (John 1:1, 14). column5: Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life (John 14:6），He fully embodies God's truth, wisdom, and revelation。 This manifestation, the “Word” (logos), existed from the beginning and became flesh to dwell among us (John 1:1, 14）。 Jesus’ structured teaching is His doctrine（***didaskalia***），and in keeping (obeying, guarding, protecting) His commandments（***entolē)*** we become His disciples（***mathētēs***）。

column4: Imagine a master architect, the greatest builder in all history, whose vision, knowledge, and wisdom surpass all others. He alone understands the perfect design for an enduring, unshakable structure. His understanding is not derived from others-it is inherent within Him. He is the source of all architectural wisdom, and every sound building finds its origin in His design. This architect represents Jesus, the Logos-the full and complete embodiment of God’s truth, wisdom, and revelation (John 1:1, John 14:6).
column5: Imagine a master architect, the greatest builder in history, whose vision, knowledge, and wisdom surpass everything。 He alone understands the perfect design of a structure that endures and cannot be shaken。 His understanding does not come from another —— rather, it is inherent in Himself。 He is the source of all architectural wisdom, and every reliable building comes from His design。 This architect represents Jesus, the Word (Logos) - the complete and perfect embodiment of God's truth, wisdom, and revelation (John 1:1, John 14:6）。

column4: To bring His design to life, the architect creates a **detailed blueprint**-a structured plan that contains the principles, proportions, and foundational truths necessary for constructing a building that will stand firm. Without this blueprint, no one could build correctly. This blueprint represents Jesus’ structured teaching, His doctrine (***didaskalia***) — the framework through which divine truth is understood and applied (Titus 2:1, 1 Timothy 4:13). His doctrine is not merely theoretical knowledge; it is the means by which His wisdom is communicated and preserved so that all who follow Him can build their lives on the right foundation.
column5: To bring His design to reality, this architect drew up a **detailed blueprint** —— a structured plan that contains the principles, proportions, and foundational truths necessary to build a sturdy structure。 Without this blueprint, no one can build correctly。 This blueprint represents Jesus’ structured teaching, that is, His doctrine（***didaskalia***） — through it, people can understand and apply the framework of divine truth (Titus 2:1, 1 Timothy 4:13）。 His doctrine is not merely theoretical knowledge; it is the way His wisdom is communicated and preserved, so that all who follow Him can build their lives on the right foundation。

column4: However, a blueprint alone is not enough. The architect also provides **precise instructions**, detailing how each part of the structure should be assembled, where each beam must be placed, and how every element should align with His perfect design. These specific instructions represent His commands **(Entolē**)-the actionable directives that govern obedience (John 14:15, Matthew 28:20). His commands are not arbitrary rules; they are the necessary steps to ensure the building stands strong, aligned with the original blueprint. To ignore or alter His commands would be to compromise the integrity of the entire structure.
column5: However, a blueprint alone is not enough。 The architect also provides **precise instructions**, detailing how each part of the structure should be assembled, where each beam should be placed, and how each element should align with His perfect design。 These specific instructions represent His commandments **(Entolē**)- executable directives that govern obedience (John 14:15, Matthew 28:20）。 His commandments are not arbitrary rules; they are the necessary steps to ensure the building is solid and aligned with the original blueprint。 To ignore or change His commandments would damage the integrity of the entire structure。

column4: Now, imagine that the architect gathers a group of **apprentices**-those who desire to learn from Him, build under His guidance, and one day teach others how to construct buildings that endure. These apprentices study His blueprint carefully, listen to His instructions attentively, and apply His commands faithfully in their work. They do not build according to their own ideas but according to the master’s design. These apprentices represent the disciples **(Mathētēs**)-those who observe, obey, and internalize Jesus’ teachings, aligning their lives with His Word (Matthew 28:19-20, John 8:31). The more they study under the architect, the more skilled they become, eventually teaching and training others in His ways.
column5: Now, imagine this architect gathering a group of **apprentices** —— those who long to learn from Him, to build under His guidance, and one day to teach others how to construct buildings that endure forever。 These apprentices carefully study His blueprint, listen attentively to His instructions, and faithfully practice His commandments in their work。 They do not build according to their own ideas, but according to the master’s design。 These apprentices represent disciples **(Mathētēs**)- those who keep, obey, and internalize Jesus’ teachings, aligning their lives with His words (Matthew 28:19-20, John 8:31）。 The more they learn under the architect’s instruction, the more skillful they become, and eventually they will also teach and train others in His way。
